name: Scorched Codex
description: Scorched Codex is a desert world whose surface is a mosaic of three distinct terrains: pale dust seas that stretch unbroken to every horizon, deep canyon systems carved by rivers that dried up millions of years ago, and vast plains of fused glass that reflect the harsh sunlight in blinding sheets. The glass plains are the planet's most striking feature—smooth, dark surfaces that formed during a cataclysmic event so intense it vitrified the surface across entire continents, preserving the landscape beneath like text sealed under a glass plate.

The thin atmosphere does nothing to soften the temperature extremes, and the transition from day to night is brutal—scorching heat gives way to bitter cold within an hour of sunset. Dust storms sweep across the plains with seasonal regularity, scouring the glass surfaces clean and depositing fine sand into the canyons in layers that build and collapse in annual cycles. Microbial life survives in the canyon depths, where moisture condenses in the shade of overhanging rock and temperatures remain within survivable range.

The ancient ruins are found on the glass plains, their foundations fused into the vitrified surface in a way that suggests they were present when the cataclysm occurred—and survived it. Their architecture is angular and spare, built from a composite material that has resisted the erosive forces that have stripped away every other surface feature over the intervening millennia. Temporal distortion zones cluster around the largest ruin complexes, creating pockets where time flows measurably faster or slower than the surrounding environment.

The temporal distortions have made archaeological study of the ruins both fascinating and dangerous—equipment left in accelerated zones ages years in hours, while researchers who linger in decelerated zones lose days without realizing it. The ruins' builders clearly understood the distortions, as their structures are oriented to avoid the worst zones while channeling foot traffic through milder ones. Scorched Codex reads like a book partially destroyed by fire—most of the text is gone, but what remains is preserved with extraordinary clarity, including the spaces between words where time itself bends.
